title: Dedekind domains

subtopics.topic: Motivation: failure of unique factorisation of elements, Kummer/Dedekind/Noether; the two families (rings of integers, smooth curves)
subtopics.sources: ideals page (Z[sqrt-5]); Corry 2017 §2-6; Conrad 'Ideal factorization' §1, §5-6; Gathmann Ch.13 intro (short, 1-2 pages each)

subtopics.topic: Discrete valuation rings: definition via valuation, uniformiser, ideals pi^k, characterisations (Noetherian local domain with principal maximal ideal; integrally closed of dim 1)
subtopics.sources: Aitken §2 (Defs 2-4, Props 5-9, Thm 11; ~8 pages, the fullest treatment); Stacks Lemma 10.119.7 (one lemma, 5 equivalent conditions); Sutherland L2 quotes the characterisation (Thm 1.16 of L1); seeds_localization DVR block
serves: common: Z_(p) and DVRs as localisations; discrete valuations
subtopics.decision: on this page (the localisation and local-rings pages point here for DVRs)

subtopics.topic: Fractional ideals, (A:I), invertible ideals; invertible implies finitely generated; invertibility is local; local: invertible iff principal; failures (Z+2iZ, (x,y) in k[x,y])
subtopics.sources: Sutherland L2 §2.5-2.6 (Def 2.13-Lemma 2.20, Ex 2.21; ~3 pages) and L3 §3.1 (Thm 3.2, Lemma 3.4, Cor 3.5); Conrad §2 (4 pages); Aitken §4-5, §7; Baanen et al. §5.2

subtopics.topic: Definition of Dedekind domain and the equivalence theorem (Noetherian+integrally closed+dim<=1; DVR localisations; all nonzero fractional ideals invertible; unique factorisation into primes), with full proofs; examples and non-examples; conventions (fields, primary definition)
subtopics.sources: Sutherland L2 Prop 2.9 + L3 Thm 3.23 (statement; proof partly deferred to problem set); Conrad §3 and §6 (Lemma 3.1/6.2, Thm 3.2/6.6: invertibility of primes, ~4 pages); Stacks Lemma 10.120.17 (factorisation implies Noetherian and DVR); Aitken Thm 64, 69; Gathmann Def 13.1, Lemma 13.3; Baanen §5.1
serves: common: examples Z[sqrt-5], PIDs, k[x,y], Z[sqrt-3], orders

subtopics.topic: Unique factorisation of ideals; the group of fractional ideals is free on the primes; valuations v_p; contain = divide; gcd = sum, lcm = intersection; primes <-> discrete valuations; geometric meaning (orders of vanishing)
subtopics.sources: Conrad §3-4 (Thm 3.6, Thm 4.3, Cor 4.5; ~5 pages); Sutherland L3 Thm 3.11, Cor 3.13 (local proof); Gathmann Prop 13.7 (primary decomposition proof), 13.13, Rem 13.11, Ex 13.12; Aitken §8 Thm 74

subtopics.topic: Chinese remainder theorem, approximation, ideals coprime to a given ideal in every class, two generators, semilocal Dedekind domains are PIDs, A/I principal ideal ring
subtopics.sources: Sutherland L3 Lemma 3.16, Cor 3.17, 3.18, 3.21, Thm 3.22 (~3 pages); Conrad §4 (Thm 4.7, Cor 4.9, Thm 4.11); Gathmann Prop 13.14
serves: common: two generators; approximation/CRT; every class contains an ideal prime to a given ideal

subtopics.topic: Absolute ideal norm N(a) = |A/a|: a/ap = A/p, multiplicativity, N((alpha)) = |N(alpha)|
subtopics.decision: on this page for the absolute norm; the relative norm N_{B/A} goes with the splitting page

subtopics.topic: Ideal class group of a domain / Dedekind domain: Pic = Cl; trivial iff PID iff UFD; Pic Z[sqrt-5] = Z/2 by a lattice argument; Claborn: every abelian group occurs; every class contains a prime for rings of integers but not in general
subtopics.sources: Sutherland L2 Def 2.22-2.23, L3 Cor 3.15; Gathmann Def 13.24, Prop 13.27, Ex 13.28; Baanen §8.1; Clark §1-2; Wikipedia
serves: core: class group, Cl trivial iff PID iff UFD
subtopics.decision: on this page for general Dedekind domains; finiteness of Cl(O_K) via Minkowski, quadratic forms and class number tables are on the existing page [[class-group]]; equidistribution/Chebotarev on [[class-field-theory]]

subtopics.topic: Localisation of Dedekind domains: S^{-1}D Dedekind; Cl(S^{-1}D) = Cl(D)/<[p] : p meets S> (Claborn); D[1/alpha]; O_K[1/alpha] vs O_K[1/N(alpha)] (corrected reading of Coykendall-Kettinger Thm 4.2); Gilmer's formula; Galois conjugation of overrings
subtopics.sources: Clark Thm 5 (proof outline); Coykendall-Kettinger §4-5 (Thm 4.1, 4.2, Cor 4.4, Prop 5.2, Ex 5.1, Thm 5.8); localization page; seeds_localization (reviewed material)
serves: common: localisation of Dedekind domains and class group of a localisation

subtopics.topic: Integral closure of a Dedekind domain in a finite separable extension is Dedekind (AKLB); rings of integers; Krull-Akizuki without separability; primes of B over primes of A and the factorisation pB = prod q^e (definitions only)
subtopics.sources: Sutherland 2015 L4 §4.5 (Props 4.55-4.60, Lemma 4.62, Thm 4.63, Rems 4.61, 4.64; ~4 pages); Baanen §7; Gathmann Prop 13.5 (Z case by finiteness of R/pR); Stacks Lemma 10.120.18
serves: core: rings of integers are Dedekind; integral closure in finite separable extension

subtopics.topic: Splitting of primes in extensions: e, f, g, sum e_i f_i = n, Dedekind-Kummer with index/conductor hypothesis, discriminant and ramification, relative norm, Galois decomposition and inertia groups, Frobenius
subtopics.sources: Sutherland 2015 L5-L7 (three lectures); Milne Ch.3 'Factorization in extensions' to 'Eisenstein extensions'; Conrad 'Factoring after Dedekind'
subtopics.decision: separate new page: 'Splitting of primes in extensions' (proposed id splitting-of-primes). It has its own definitions (e, f, g, decomposition and inertia groups), its own main theorems (fundamental identity, Dedekind-Kummer, ramification and discriminant) and its own lectures/chapter in every text. This page gives only the definition of primes lying over p and of e, f, with one worked example; Dedekind-Kummer for quadratic fields is already stated on [[ideals]].

subtopics.topic: Finiteness of the class group of O_K (Minkowski bound), class group computations
subtopics.sources: Milne Ch.4; Sutherland 2015 L13; Conrad 'Class group calculations'; Baanen §8.2 (alternative)
serves: common: finiteness of the class group
subtopics.decision: existing page [[class-group]] (Minkowski bound, reduced forms); this page states the theorem, explains why it is special to global fields (Claborn), and links

subtopics.topic: Finitely generated modules over a Dedekind domain: ideals projective, I + J = A + IJ, torsion-free = A^{n-1} + I, Steinitz class
subtopics.sources: UW Math 505 notes 'Lecture 2-26' (2025) (complete proofs); Gargava et al. §2 Def 7, Prop 9; Wikipedia
subtopics.decision: on this page, as a short final section with the key proofs (it is how papers such as Gargava et al. use the class group)

subtopics.topic: Geometric Dedekind domains: smooth affine curves, Pic and the group law of a cubic, Pic k[E] = E(k), non-replete domains
subtopics.decision: on this page as examples and a views item; the theory of curves belongs to [[algebraic-varieties]] / [[riemann-roch]]

subtopics.topic: Factorisation theory (Krull monoids, transfer to zero-sum sequences, half-factoriality, sets of lengths)
subtopics.decision: not covered here beyond a statement and an example of non-unique lengths; see [gg]. A future page 'Factorisation theory of Krull monoids' could take it.

subtopics.topic: Narrow and ray class groups, Hilbert class field
Computational class groups (S-units, factor bases, Bach bound, Smith normal form); Ore/Montes
Orders: non-invertible primes, conductor, Pic of an order
subtopics.sources: Conrad §8; Sutherland L2 Ex 2.21; Chang-Geroldinger §4 Cor 9
subtopics.decision: non-examples (Z+2iZ, Z[sqrt-3]) on this page; Pic of orders and the exact sequence not covered here, see [gg] §4 and [conrad] §8

page_order: 3 Dedekind domains: definition, examples and the equivalence theorem
4 Unique factorisation of ideals and valuations
5 Chinese remainder theorem, approximation and two generators
9 Rings of integers and integral closures
notes: Fields: we follow Sutherland/Gathmann-style statements but allow fields where harmless and say so in a conventions block.
Chang-Geroldinger do not state that Pic of a localisation is a quotient (checked); that statement is cited to Clark Thm 5 and Coykendall-Kettinger Thm 4.1 instead.
Coykendall-Kettinger Thm 4.2 is reproduced in its corrected reading (seeds_localization).
Coykendall-Kettinger Example 6.3 (36 primes in distinct classes) is not used.
Milne could not be read beyond Ch.2 and is not cited for content.
